sources.citation: Bruce, Les. 1984. The Alamblak language of Papua New Guinea (East Sepik). Pacific Linguistics C-81.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Published version of Bruce 1979; only relevant as the best-described Sepik Hill relative (Alamblak stress rules), not for Mari itself. Open at ANU (handle 1885/145229).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mari language (Sepik)' (accessed 2026-09-17; cites Ethnologue 25th ed. and Global Recordings Network).
sources.note: Nothing; ~80 speakers, Mari village, Gawi Rural LLG; GRN audio recordings exist.

sources.citation: Laycock, Don. 1991. Three vowels, semivowels, and neutralisation: orthographic and other problems of Sepik languages. PL A-73: 107-114.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not mention Mari; general Sepik vowel/orthography discussion only.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert & Ron Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (PL A-76): 243-274, section 4.2 Sepik Hill Stock/Family.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Mari is only listed among Sepik Hill languages (Bruce 1979 / Wurm 1982 subgroupings).

sources.citation: Bruce, Leslie P., Jr. 1979. A grammar of Alamblak (Papua New Guinea). PhD thesis, Australian National University. pp. 23-24 (data sources) and comparative Sepik Hill chapter pp. 472-519.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress-placement rules (ch. on phonology, pp. ~97ff.) are for Alamblak only. Mari enters only as comparative wordlist data taken from Dye et al. 1968 ('the data for six languages consist of word lists collected by Dye, et al. (1968). These languages are Kaningara, Kapriman-Karambit, Watakataui, Bisis, Mari, and Bitara'); no statement about Mari stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page mari1432 (subclassification refs Bruce 1979: 472-519; Haberland & Seyfarth 1974: 24; AES status shifting; links to Ethnologue, OLAC, ELP).
sources.note: Nothing; no descriptive (grammar/sketch/phonology) reference is listed for the language — only overview/wordlist/classification items.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. Entry 101 MARI, p. 29 (PDF p. 33).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives only village (Mari, CD 44E), population (120) and a comment that Dye & Townsends' figure of 147 suggests uncensused hamlets; no linguistic data at all.

sources.citation: Unpublished SIL-PNG wordlists and survey notes held by the project at Ukarumpa for Sepik Hill languages (referred to by Bruce 1979: 24).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Bruce reports SIL wordlists for Sepik Hill languages held by the project in Ukarumpa; a Mari survey wordlist with marked stress would be the only conceivable first-hand data. SIL resource pages for mbx could not be downloaded (not reachable by automated download).

sources.citation: Haberland, Eike & Siegfried Seyfarth. 1974. Die Yimar am oberen Korowori (Neuguinea). Wiesbaden: Franz Steiner.

sources.note: Ethnography of the Yimar (Karawari) area with a classification comment on Mari (p. 24, per Glottolog); might include a short vocabulary but is not a linguistic description.

sources.citation: Dye, Wayne, Patricia Townsend & William Townsend. 1968. The Sepik Hill languages: a preliminary report. Oceania 39(2): 146-156.

sources.note: The only primary field data on Mari (wordlists, lexicostatistics); an 11-page preliminary report may contain a paragraph of phonological notes on the Sepik Hill languages. Every later mention of Mari (Laycock 1973, Bruce 1979, Conrad & Lewis 1988) derives from it.
